scope: Remix 3.1 documentation and package APIs. This is the new Remix component/Fetch architecture, not React-based Remix v2 or React Router framework mode.

ssr.note: The closure-based component runtime renders server HTML, selectively hydrates clientEntry components, and can create browser roots. It does not use React.

streaming.note: Frame can stream fallback HTML first and reconcile a route-owned HTML region when it resolves. Frames can also reload through separate browser requests; components themselves are synchronous.
streaming.label: Streaming Frames

suspense.note: Frame can stream fallback HTML first and reconcile a route-owned HTML region when it resolves. Frames can also reload through separate browser requests; components themselves are synchronous.
suspense.label: Streaming Frames

client.note: The closure-based component runtime renders server HTML, selectively hydrates clientEntry components, and can create browser roots. It does not use React.

ssg.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix rendering guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

csr.note: The closure-based component runtime renders server HTML, selectively hydrates clientEntry components, and can create browser roots. It does not use React.

serverOnly.note: Only explicitly declared client entries hydrate; ordinary server component code need not become a browser entry.

partialRendering.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix rendering guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

routing.note: Typed routes and Fetch controllers match URLs, handle HTTP methods, compose middleware and return standard Responses including redirects.

layouts.note: Shared Document/layout components receive nested children explicitly. This satisfies layout composition without a filesystem-selected layout convention.
layouts.label: Explicit layouts

dynamicRoutes.note: Typed routes and Fetch controllers match URLs, handle HTTP methods, compose middleware and return standard Responses including redirects.

parallelRoutes.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix routing guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

interceptedRoutes.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix routing guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

prefetch.note: The link mixin supports navigation prefetching; frame navigation reconciles route HTML.

softNavigation.note: Remix 3.1's run() runtime handles eligible links/forms as frame navigation and reconciles server HTML, with navigation/scroll/focus handling. This is the new Remix frame runtime, not Remix v2's React Router integration.
softNavigation.label: Remix 3 frames

viewTransitions.note: Remix 3.1 documents component enter/exit/list animation helpers, but the reviewed guide does not establish a coordinated page-navigation animation API. Remix v2 React Router viewTransition examples do not establish support in Remix 3.

redirects.note: Typed routes and Fetch controllers match URLs, handle HTTP methods, compose middleware and return standard Responses including redirects.

serverData.note: Route actions load and validate data before passing props into synchronous components.

clientData.note: Named Frames reload and reconcile server HTML, preserving matching client state. This is not an application query cache.
clientData.label: Frame reloads

requestDedupe.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix data guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

persistentCache.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix data guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

invalidation.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix data guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

isr.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix data guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

apiRoutes.note: Typed routes and Fetch controllers match URLs, handle HTTP methods, compose middleware and return standard Responses including redirects.

httpErrors.note: Unmatched routes return 404; route actions return explicit error Responses for missing records and other expected failures. Unexpected router exceptions need a server-boundary catch or the Node adapter’s onError hook to produce 500 before bytes are sent. Stream render errors use explicit hooks; after publication they cannot replace the response status.
httpErrors.label: Fetch statuses; server boundary

actions.note: Controller actions handle named HTTP routes and enhanced forms. A generated arbitrary function-call RPC boundary is not established.
actions.label: Controller actions

forms.note: Route form helpers, form-data middleware and data-schema validation support ordinary and enhanced submissions.

assessment.summary: Form transport, validation, pending feedback and optimistic state are separate behaviors; the progressive-forms and optimistic-updates rows review the latter contracts explicitly.
strengths: Route form helpers, form-data middleware and data-schema validation support ordinary and enhanced submissions.
tradeoffs: Do not infer a no-JavaScript submission path, automatic validation, accessible field errors or rollback merely from the ability to receive FormData.

middleware.note: Typed routes and Fetch controllers match URLs, handle HTTP methods, compose middleware and return standard Responses including redirects.

cookies.note: Cookie/session, authentication and CSRF middleware are provided as Remix modules; applications must configure stores, strategies and protection on their routes. The narrative chapter is unfinished; linked package APIs are the authority.

cssModules.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix styling guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

scopedCss.note: The css mixin supplies component-scoped styles, nested selectors, dynamic values and cascade layers.

tailwind.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix styling guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

cssInJs.note: The css mixin supplies component-scoped styles, nested selectors, dynamic values and cascade layers.

images.note: The documented transform pipeline uses optional Sharp for image resizing/encoding; Sharp is installed separately.
images.label: Sharp transforms

fonts.note: Font files can be served and preloaded through asset URLs. Automatic subsetting and fallback metrics are not established.
fonts.label: Asset files / preloads

scripts.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix assets guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

assetPipeline.note: Remix 3’s asset server compiles scripts and styles and serves file assets. Content-based fingerprinted URLs are optional; stable URLs use ETags and revalidation by default. Enable fingerprinting and its URL generation for long-lived caching; this is the Remix 3 API, not the older React-based Remix build pipeline.
assetPipeline.label: Optional fingerprinted URLs

staticAssets.note: The asset server compiles browser source on demand, exposes controlled files/packages, supports fingerprinting and live code updates.

metadata.note: An application-owned Document component receives title/data and authors head tags. No structured metadata field-merging registry is established.
metadata.label: Document props

dynamicMetadata.note: An application-owned Document component receives title/data and authors head tags. No structured metadata field-merging registry is established.
dynamicMetadata.label: Document props

metadataInheritance.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix metadata guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

metadataOverrides.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix metadata guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

titleTemplates.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix metadata guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

socialImages.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix metadata guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

sitemaps.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix metadata guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

robots.note: staticFiles serves an authored robots.txt; directive generation is application-owned.
robots.label: Static file

markdown.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix content guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

collections.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix content guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

translations.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix i18n guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

localeRouting.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix i18n guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

localeFormatting.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix i18n guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

auth.note: Authentication primitives include credentials, external providers and extensible strategies. Account persistence and authorization remain application policy.

csp.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix security guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

cspNonce.note: The reviewed security/rendering API does not establish coordinated per-response CSP nonces for generated scripts and styles. Hash-based CSP and application-authored headers are different mechanisms.

csrf.note: csrf middleware supports token sources and origin validation. Register it on the relevant routes and follow the cookie/session caveats.

environment.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix security guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

types.note: Typed APIs and remix commands support project development, asset inspection and database lifecycle operations. Compilation does not replace TypeScript type checking.

hmr.note: The asset server compiles browser source on demand, exposes controlled files/packages, supports fingerprinting and live code updates.

cli.note: Typed APIs and remix commands support project development, asset inspection and database lifecycle operations. Compilation does not replace TypeScript type checking.

bundleAnalysis.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix tooling guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

unitTests.note: Remix's test tooling exercises Fetch controllers, components and application behavior; the reviewed guide links runnable package examples.

e2eTests.note: remix/test has an e2e runner and server lifecycle helpers driven through Playwright; browser component tests run in isolated browser frames.

observability.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix testing guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

errorHandling.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix testing guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

serverHosting.note: The documented Node Fetch adapter serves router.fetch. The production chapter is unfinished, so deployment configuration and operations remain application-owned.

subpathProxy.note: The Node Fetch adapter can opt in to trusted forwarding headers for public origin/client information. Typed route patterns and application middleware supply routing, but the application must coordinate a mount prefix with links, asset-server URLs and the proxy. The adapter’s proxy support alone is not automatic whole-app rebasing.
subpathProxy.label: Fetch adapter; app-owned mount

staticHosting.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix deployment guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

containers.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix deployment guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

edgeHosting.note: Not established in the reviewed Remix deployment guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

orm.note: data-table supplies typed relational queries, transactional operations, and journaled up/down SQL migrations. Database drivers are separate dependencies.
orm.label: data-table

assessment.summary: An ORM/query API establishes a data-access surface, not identical relationship loading, N+1 detection, migration or encryption behavior.
strengths: data-table supplies typed relational queries, transactional operations, and journaled up/down SQL migrations. Database drivers are separate dependencies.
tradeoffs: Review eager loading, query counts and transaction semantics for the selected driver. Schema migrations, transactions and encrypted fields are compared separately.

migrations.note: data-table supplies typed relational queries, transactional operations, and journaled up/down SQL migrations. Database drivers are separate dependencies.
migrations.label: data-table

transactions.note: data-table supplies typed relational queries, transactional operations, and journaled up/down SQL migrations. Database drivers are separate dependencies.
transactions.label: data-table

jobs.note: The reviewed Remix server/data guides do not establish an owned background jobs API. An application can integrate a separate provider or library; this finding does not mean that integration is impossible.

mail.note: The reviewed Remix server/data guides do not establish an owned email API. An application can integrate a separate provider or library; this finding does not mean that integration is impossible.

uploads.note: Multipart parsing, streaming uploads, size limits and file-storage APIs include local and S3-compatible storage.

realtime.note: The reviewed Remix server/data guides do not establish an owned real-time delivery API. An application can integrate a separate provider or library; this finding does not mean that integration is impossible.

xssEscaping.note: remix/html-template escapes interpolated values and composes branded SafeHtml without double escaping. html.raw is an explicit trusted-output bypass; this HTML-encoding policy does not establish arbitrary script/URL safety or rich-HTML sanitization.
xssEscaping.label: HTML templates / trusted raw bypass

htmlSanitization.note: The linked security API review does not establish the specific html sanitization contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

authorization.note: The linked security API review does not establish the specific authorization policies contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

rateLimiting.note: The linked security API review does not establish the specific rate limiting contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

progressiveEnhancement.note: The router guide demonstrates ordinary HTML forms posted to server handlers, followed by useful HTML responses. Enhanced component forms are separate; a browser-only handler must not replace the real submission path if no-JS behavior is required.
progressiveEnhancement.label: Native form handlers

optimisticUi.note: The linked data API review does not establish the specific optimistic updates contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

requestCancellation.note: A newer frame reload cancels earlier client work for that frame, including pending requests and streamed content. Server work may already have happened; cancellation is not mutation rollback.
requestCancellation.label: Frame reload cancellation

typedLinks.note: Typed route maps expose href construction with route parameter inference for links and form destinations. This is Remix 3's Fetch/router API, not React Router type generation.
typedLinks.label: Typed route maps

searchParams.note: The linked routing API review does not establish the specific validated url state contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

stateRestoration.note: Frame reconciliation preserves matching client component state while updating server HTML. State survives only while component identity is retained; durable restoration after reload or replacement is application-owned.
stateRestoration.label: Frame reconciliation

scrollRestoration.note: The linked routing API review does not establish the specific scroll restoration contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

navigationBlocking.note: The linked routing API review does not establish the specific unsaved-change guards contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

navigationAccessibility.note: The frame navigation runtime resets focus and scroll by default and provides explicit resetFocus/resetScroll controls. This is focus behavior, not a documented SvelteKit-style route announcer or a general accessibility guarantee.
navigationAccessibility.label: Navigation focus controls

a11yChecks.note: The linked client rendering API review does not establish the specific accessibility checks contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

httpTests.note: Fetch-style handlers can be called with Request objects and their Responses asserted without an HTTP listener. This is the documented Fetch-handler boundary, not an attributed Rails-style session test DSL.
httpTests.label: Fetch handler tests
